requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/01-overview-page-018.tex:4
requirements.statement: Federates use the state of the object instances as one of the primary means of communication. At any point during a federation execution, at most one federate or the RTI shall have the privilege to update the value of a given object instance attribute. A joined federate that has the privilege to update values for an instance attribute is said to own that instance attribute. There are specific (MOM) instance attributes that are owned by the RTI. In some cases, an instance attribute may be unowned, neither owned by a federate nor the RTI. The Ownership Management services allow joined federates to gain ownership of unowned instance attributes, exchange ownership of instance attributes, or release ownership of instance attributes (possibly to become unowned). The federate provides instance attribute values to the other federates in the federation execution via Object Management services. The federate providing the instance attribute values is said to be updating that instance attribute. Federates receiving those values are said to be reflecting that instance attribute.

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/01-overview-page-019.tex:11
requirements.statement: Some of the arguments to the services described in this document are in the form of a group that represents some association. These groupings can take several forms (depending on the requirements of the respective service), each of which is described below. The groupings may be implemented slightly differently in each API, but all implementations shall support the same semantics. These groupings are pairs, sets, collections, constrained sets of pairs, and collections of pairs. Collections are sets that permit duplication of elements. They are used in cases in which duplication is unlikely and not really an error. As such, using a collection rather than a set retains the same effects, but without the expensive checks to eliminate duplicates that using a set would require. In these cases, it is preferred not to penalize the majority of users with the less efficient set just to catch errors that are anticipated to be infrequent.

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/04-federation-management-page-038.tex:27
requirements.statement: The exact manner in which RTI-initiated services (callbacks) are invoked on a federate by the RTI is programming-language specific. However, the HLA defines two callback models that govern when callbacks may be invoked. The two callback models are: IMMEDIATE and EVOKED. In the IMMEDIATE model, the RTI shall invoke callbacks immediately when they are available, unless the callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. In the EVOKED model, callbacks are only made when the federate calls the Evoke Callback/Evoke Multiple Callbacks services, unless callbacks have been disabled using the Disable Callbacks service. RTIs shall implement both callback models. The callback model is specified as an argument to the Connect service.

The federate name argument shall be unique within a federation execution at any given time. It may, however, be assigned to a different federate after a restore operation. The returned joined federate designator shall be unique for the lifetime of the federation execution as long as a restore is not in progress at any federate. If the RTI is configured to require authorization, the RTI shall require that the credentials provided in the Connect service invocation allows for joining the named federation execution using the provided federate name and type.

requirements.title: Normative statement at content/clauses/07-ownership-management-page-175.tex:29
requirements.statement: Logical time in the system being modeled shall be represented in the federation as points along the time axis with an initial and final point. A logical time represents a single point on the time axis. A logical time interval represents the distance between two points on the time axis. A joined federate can associate both itself and some of its activities with logical times. A joined federate’s association with a logical time is referred to as the time position of the joined federate. An association of a joined federate’s activities with logical times is denoted by assigning timestamps to the messages representing those activities. Timestamps and time position are both represented by the same logical time data type and, therefore, can be compared, but they are referenced using different terms in order to help clarify whether a given logical time value applies to a joined federate or to a joined federate’s activities. A logical time interval is a separate data type used by time-regulating federates to specify a lookahead and by the RTI to perform arithmetic operations with logical time values.

requirements.statement: Federates advancing via the Flush Queue Grant service in response to a Flush Request Grant service shall be provided with a supplemental optimistic logical time in addition to a logical time. The optimistic logical time is the minimum of the time supplied in a Flush Queue Grant and the timestamps of any TSO messages delivered in response to that Flush Queue Grant. The consideration of delivered TSO messages does not exclude those specified in Request Retraction service calls. The optimistic logical time indicates a lower bound on the next logical time the federate could be advanced to if no TSO messages with a timestamp less than it are received in the future. Federates that have advanced as a result of the Flush Queue Grant service are further restricted by the optimistic logical time when making the next time advance. The federate may request to advance only to a logical time that is greater than or equal to its optimistic logical time.
